summary: Charging speed at station #789 is extremely slow
description: Multiple users have reported that charging station #789 is charging at a significantly reduced speed (around 3kW instead of the expected 7kW). The issue seems to be persistent throughout the day.

comments.author: John Doe, Site Reliability Engineer
comments.comment: Initial investigation shows no hardware faults. Power output from the grid is stable. Could this be a firmware issue?

comments.author: Jane Smith, Firmware Engineer
comments.comment: We pushed a new firmware update (v2.3.1) last week. It's possible that a new power management feature is too aggressive. Rolling back the firmware on this station to v2.3.0 for testing.

comments.author: John Doe, Site Reliability Engineer
comments.comment: RCA: The firmware update v2.3.1 introduced a bug in the thermal throttling logic, causing the station to prematurely reduce power output. The issue was resolved by applying a hotfix (v2.3.2) that corrects the throttling curve.

summary: Payment terminal on station #456 is frozen
description: The payment terminal on station #456 is unresponsive. The screen is frozen on the "Welcome" message, and it does not respond to touch or card swipes. A remote reboot of the station did not resolve the issue.

comments.author: Support Team
comments.comment: A technician has been dispatched to the site to perform a hard reboot of the payment terminal.

comments.author: Field Operations
comments.comment: Technician confirmed that a hard reboot resolved the issue. This seems to be a recurring problem with this model of payment terminal. We should investigate the root cause.

comments.author: Firmware Team
comments.comment: RCA: The payment terminal's memory was exhausted due to a memory leak in the card reader driver. A firmware update for the payment terminal is required. As a temporary workaround, a nightly reboot has been scheduled for all stations with this terminal model.

description: Station #101 has been offline for the past 2 hours. It is not responding to remote commands, and it is not sending any heartbeats.

comments.author: Network Operations
comments.comment: The station is located in an area with known cellular connectivity issues. It's possible that the modem has lost its connection.

comments.author: Support Team
comments.comment: A local technician has been asked to check the physical status of the station and the modem.

comments.author: Hardware Team
comments.comment: RCA: The cellular modem had entered a fault state and was not able to reconnect to the network. A power cycle of the modem resolved the issue. We are investigating a permanent solution to make the modem more resilient to network fluctuations.

description: Attempted to update firmware on station #321 from v2.3.2 to v2.4.0, but the update failed. The station is now reporting a 'FirmwareUpdateFailed' status.

comments.author: Support Team
comments.comment: Customer support initiated a remote firmware update, which failed. The station is currently operational on the old firmware, but the new features are not available.

comments.author: QA Engineer
comments.comment: I am trying to reproduce this in the lab. Can you provide the logs from the failed update attempt? I am also checking the release notes for v2.4.0 for any known issues.

comments.author: Developer
comments.comment: The logs show a 'SignatureMismatch' error. It seems the firmware signature verification failed. This could be due to a corrupted firmware file or an issue with the signing key. I am investigating the build process for v2.4.0.

description: A security audit has identified a potential vulnerability in the TLS implementation of the charging station firmware. The station may be susceptible to a man-in-the-middle attack.

comments.author: Security Team
comments.comment: We have identified that the firmware is not correctly validating the Central System's certificate chain. This is a critical vulnerability and needs to be addressed immediately.

comments.author: Developer
comments.comment: I am reviewing the TLS handshake code. It seems we are not properly handling certificate pinning. I am working on a patch.

comments.author: QA Engineer
comments.comment: I will set up a test environment to reproduce the man-in-the-middle attack and validate the patch once it is ready.

summary: Race condition in SpoolerVaultAuth during initialization
description: Under heavy load, concurrent requests to `api_key_from_machine_id` can cause an `InvalidPath` exception from the Vault client. This happens if the secrets engine at `spooler/stations` is not yet fully mounted when the first requests arrive.

comments.author: Chayan Mazumder, Platform Engineer
comments.comment: This appears to be a startup race condition. The `on_startup` hook initializes Vault, but web requests can arrive before it's complete. We need a locking mechanism.

comments.author: Jane Smith, Developer
comments.comment: I've reproduced this locally. I'm working on a fix in PR #4567 that adds a lock and retry logic to the `api_key_from_machine_id` method. This should make the service more robust during cold starts.
